problem.summary: A light-side formal-evidence guard already existed, but its critical-fail mapping used aliases that did not match the canonical Visual Fidelity Gate IDs, it was not explicitly bound into the core gate-integrity entry point, and it still allowed stable-but-artificial sun-side state such as a cookie, flare, ForceVertex render mode or selective layer mask. Camera-side purity alone cannot exclude those lighting/shadow injection paths.
riskToGate: Alias critical IDs could let the light-purity policy drift away from the exact 12-defect gate vocabulary.
Light command buffers are already forbidden, but a directional cookie or flare could still alter formal pixels without changing camera post-processing state.
A ForceVertex key or selective directional culling mask could produce materially inconsistent lighting while remaining stable from pre-cull to post-render.
If light-purity validation were only callback-driven, reflection-probe baselines could be requested before the MainCamera callbacks ever run.

implementation.change: Raised the contract to schema 1.1, replaced alias critical mappings with the exact canonical gate IDs, and made sun cookie, flare, ForceVertex lighting and reduced culling masks explicitly forbidden.

Requires exact-set equality for the canonical critical IDs; rejects SummerSun cookie, flare, ForceVertex mode, selective culling and shadow disablement; and expands the formal-light-state hash to include subtractive shadow color, pixelLightCount, shadowmaskMode, renderMode, cookieSize and flare identity/dependency state.
Binds the light-purity contract into the core Visual Fidelity Gate integrity entry point, so direct gate/packet paths cannot accept a weakened or alias-mapped light policy.

Adds explicit light-purity contract preflight and scene validation immediately before reflection synchronization, before native still capture, and again before prepared temporal capture. Per-frame pre-cull/pre-render/post-render callbacks remain the runtime guard.

issuesFoundAndCorrected.issue: The existing light contract used inconsistent_sun_shadow_direction, severe_aliasing_or_shimmering and claiming_render_quality_without_actual_render, while the canonical gate uses sun_shadow_inconsistency, severe_aliasing_or_shimmer and unverified_render_claim.
issuesFoundAndCorrected.correction: Changed the contract and validator to exact canonical IDs and exact-set equality instead of loose Contains checks.

issuesFoundAndCorrected.issue: The next planned work item was initially described as adding a Light command-buffer audit, but source inspection showed that audit already existed.
issuesFoundAndCorrected.correction: Avoided duplicating the existing implementation and instead hardened its uncovered state channels and gate integration.

sourceDataChecks: BuildQualityBlock1990s creates one SummerSun directional light and a park-lamp Point Light whose intensity is 0, so the intended daytime scene model is compatible with the active-emitter rule.
The existing guard already audits every scene Light, including disabled lights, across all LightEvent command-buffer attachment points.
The existing formal target vocabulary remains QA4K_ and QAPreparedTemporal_ at native 3840x2160.
The new contract awards zero Visual Fidelity points and retains UNSCORED_REVIEW_REQUIRED until actual pixels exist.

Unity 6 API documentation was checked for LightEvent/commandBufferCount, pixelLightCount, shadowmaskMode and Light cookie/culling/flare/renderMode properties; compile/runtime verification is still pending.

expectedVisualScoreImpact.expectedEffectAfterRealRender: No visual point is earned by this evidence-integrity change. It reduces the chance that formal 4K/temporal evidence is accepted after hidden light-side injection or after the light QA vocabulary drifts away from the canonical gate.
